content_html:
A Revised Haskell 2010 Language Report

David Binder August 04, 2026 [Ecosystem] #haskell-2010

The Haskell 2010 language report was released almost exactly 16 years ago, and although various attempts have been made, no further report has been released. This does not mean, however, that the language hasn't changed. On the contrary, the Haskell that we write today is quite different to the one we wrote 16 years ago, and the language has become more beautiful, consistent and ergonomic in the process. The specification, unfortunately, couldn't keep up.

Many members of our community express some pessimism when it comes to the possibility of a new report. Sure, they would also love to have a new and updated report, but they think that it is either too hard or not worth the effort. I think that is not true. Having an up-to-date report is essential for the health of our community, and it is actually possible for us to get there in a reasonable amount of time with a reasonable amount of work. Here is my plan for how we can get there, and how we can finish the process before the new year.

Why We Need a New Report

The Haskell Language Report is an essential part of the documentation of the language. It is not the first thing that a beginner should consult when they learn Haskell, but it is an important resource for those who want to advance to being an intermediate or experienced Haskeller. If you want to learn about the precise syntax of floating point literals, the rules and desugaring for do-notation, or the meaning of default declarations, the report is the authorative resource where you can find answers. It is therefore unfortunate if the answers that you find in the report are wrong, or do not correspond to what compilers implement or the base library provides. In that case, you have to retrace the proposals and discussions that lead to the current state: The Functor-Applicative-Monad, MonadFail, Foldable-Traversable and Monad-of-no-return proposals undoubtedly made the language better, but they also turn programmers looking for answers in the report into involuntary Haskell historians.

If the language report were the only Haskell resource available to you, then any non-trivial Haskell 2010 program that you would write is almost guaranteed to be incompatible with what modern compilers like GHC or MicroHS expect. We can, and should, fix that.

How to Get the Cost-Benefit Tradeoff Right

Writing a new report is a lot of work, and we want to avoid running into the problems that stalled previous attempts of writing one. It is therefore important that we set ourselves a goal that is both achievable and provides a tangible benefit for the Haskell community. The most obvious such goal is to start with a Revised Haskell 2010 Language Report:

  • A revised report is eminently achievable: We have a very clear "todo list" in the documented discrepancies in the user guide (GHC User Guide: Bugs and Infelicities). Most of these listed discrepancies are already well-documented in the accepted proposals that lead to them.
  • None of the changes that we have to implement are likely to be contentious: They reflect the Haskell that we are already writing today. Since the required changes are not contentious, we can use a lightweight decision process in the compilation of the revised report.
  • There is a clear benefit for the community: The most important piece of our reference documentation is no longer outdated. We can refer people to the Haskell report without having to warn them to stay clear of parts of the report that no longer hold true.
  • Since we don't define a new Haskell version with a new feature set, but only a revised version of a previous report, we don't generate any churn for the ecosystem or compiler writers. Taking inspiration from Tolkien who rewrote the Hobbit after he came up with the story of the Lord of the Rings, we can retcon the report and pretend that the revised report is what we meant by Haskell2010 all along. We can then simplify the GHC user guide and remove most of its section 16 which documents infelicities compared to the existing report.

So here is the a target that we can set for ourselves: Every program that is valid according to the revised Haskell 2010 language report will be accepted by MicroHS and GHC using the Haskell2010 language edition.

Let's Talk Technicalities

With the motivation and goal out of the way, let us discuss some technical details when it comes to working on the report, building it, and generating the final PDF and HTML documents.

The Haskell 2010 language report is available both as a PDF and HTML document, and there are no obvious good reasons to change this. Working on a document of the complexity and length of the Haskell report can be made joyful if the authoring technology is right, and arduous if we are struggling with long compile times (Compiling long-ish PDFs with LaTeX can take minutes using the wrong tools and packages!), inscrutable error messages or a difficult scripting and programming model.

The previous version of the Haskell report was written using a combination of command line tools (sed, awk, perl, make), a lexer/parser for preprocessing a custom .verb file format, pdflatex to compile the PDF, and tex4ht to generate HTML. In 2026 we can use technology that was not available in 2010 and simplify the process of authoring the report significantly. Of the available technologies, the Typst typesetting system currently satisfies the constraints the best:

  • It is open-source software available under the Apache 2.0 license. (An associated cloud service similar to Overleaf is proprietary, but entirely optional.)
  • Typst is implemented in Rust and has compile times that are roughly an order of magnitude faster than tex. This allows to get instantaneous visual feedback when working on the report.
  • Both PDF and HTML output is supported natively, with no need to use separate tools.
  • The compiler emits fantastic error messages which point to the erroneous location in the code.
  • Simpler technologies (like plain Markdown) also allow to target multiple output formats, but they lack the advanced features to generate high-quality technical documentation, especially when it comes to the typesetting of mathematics and complex figures.

Using Typst means we have to convert the report from the custom .verb format to .typ files; fortunately this part of the work is completed, and the report can be compiled using a simple typst compile invocation. (The translation process did not involve LLMs, and was done manually using some sed and awk magic to facilitate the process.) Re-typesetting the BNF grammars also allowed to make them hyperlinked: It is now possible to navigate the grammar by clicking on non-terminal symbols and to jump to their definition.

Documenting the Standard Libraries

The existing Haskell 2010 report consists of two parts: The first part documents the syntax and semantics of the language, and the second part documents the standard libraries. Documenting the standard libraries is an essential part of the report, because many aspects of the language can only be defined in terms of functions, types and type classes available in the libraries. For example, numeric literals are polymorphic and have to be defined in terms of the numeric hierarchy, do-notation has to be defined in terms of the Monad (and MonadFail) type classes, and the foreign function interface (FFI) makes extensive use of functions and types defined in the Foreign.* namespace.

Maintaining hundreds of pages of standard library documentation in purely textual form (either as LaTeX or Typst files), and ensuring that they remain valid Haskell and consistent with each other is very hard. If we want to avoid typos and inconsistencies sneeking into the report, and if we want to keep the library specification maintainable, then we have to organize it in some form which is amenable to machine checking. The obvious solution is to document the API of the standard libraries using Haddock. The repository for the revised report contains a cabal package which exposes the precise API specified in the Haskell 2010 language report. (This package only specifies the public API: The functions and methods themselves do not have an implementation. A possible stretch goal would be to use tools like api-diff or print-api (Link) to ensure that the API exposed by packages like base is a strict superset of the API defined in the report.)

What Process Shall we Use

The Haskell Prime process worked using a combination of mailing list discussions and a Git repository which collected RFCs. Notably, the process did not work directly on the source code used for building the report. We can reduce a lot of the overhead by switching to a collaboration process that is modelled more closely on how we develop code: Changes to the report should primarily be discussed in the form of pull requests to the textual sources of the report itself. The repository to organize the writing of the report is now public: github.com/haskellfoundation/haskell-2010-revised-report. Please start contributing by discussing the existing issues, by contributing new issues, and by helping fix issues with the technical infrastructure. We will not yet merge any actual changes to the report, since these changes will need to be confirmed by the new language committee that will be established, but we can start working on all other technical issues.

Call to Action

In order for the revised Haskell 2010 report to enjoy broad support from the community, we have established a new working group under the umbrella of the Haskell Foundation. We now need your help and participation, ideally by deciding to become a member of the working group tasked with compiling the revised report. If you do not want to become a member of the working group you can still join all the discussions in the repository, contribute issues, and open pull requests with changes to the report, but becoming a member gives you the right to cast your vote on which changes to the report shall be adopted.

We will shortly be announcing a call to join the working group on the Haskell Discourse, and soon thereafter start the work on the revised report. If you always wished for Haskell to get a new report, or were discouraged by the lack of progress when it comes to standardization, now is your chance to contribute! With the clearly delimited scope set out above we can also be confident that the finish line is clearly in sight. And who knows, if the revised report is a clear success we might even have the appetite to follow up with something more ambitious...

sentences.en: Documenting the Standard Libraries

blocks.html_en: The existing Haskell 2010 report consists of two parts: The first part documents the syntax and semantics of the language, and the second part documents the standard libraries. Documenting the standard libraries is an essential part of the report, because many aspects of the language can only be defined in terms of functions, types and type classes available in the libraries. For example, numeric literals are polymorphic and have to be defined in terms of the numeric hierarchy, do-notation has to be defined in terms of the Monad (and MonadFail) type classes, and the foreign function interface (FFI) makes extensive use of functions and types defined in the Foreign.* namespace.

blocks.html_en: Maintaining hundreds of pages of standard library documentation in purely textual form (either as LaTeX or Typst files), and ensuring that they remain valid Haskell and consistent with each other is very hard. If we want to avoid typos and inconsistencies sneeking into the report, and if we want to keep the library specification maintainable, then we have to organize it in some form which is amenable to machine checking. The obvious solution is to document the API of the standard libraries using Haddock. The repository for the revised report contains a cabal package which exposes the precise API specified in the Haskell 2010 language report. (This package only specifies the public API: The functions and methods themselves do not have an implementation. A possible stretch goal would be to use tools like api-diff or print-api (Link) to ensure that the API exposed by packages like base is a strict superset of the API defined in the report.)

We can reduce a lot of the overhead by switching to a collaboration process that is modelled more closely on how we develop code: Changes to the report should primarily be discussed in the form of pull requests to the textual sources of the report itself. The repository to organize the writing of the report is now public: github.com/haskellfoundation/haskell-2010-revised-report. Please start contributing by discussing the existing issues, by contributing new issues, and by helping fix issues with the technical infrastructure. content_html_zh:
修订后的 Haskell 2010 语言报告

David Binder August 04, 2026 [Ecosystem] #haskell-2010

Haskell 2010语言报告几乎正好是在16年前发布的，尽管进行了各种尝试，但还没有发布进一步的报告。 然而，这并不意味着语言没有改变。 相反，我们今天编写的 Haskell 与我们 16 年前编写的 Haskell 有很大不同，并且在这个过程中语言变得更加美观、一致和符合人体工程学。 不幸的是，该规范无法跟上。

当谈到新报告的可能性时，我们社区的许多成员表达了一些悲观情绪。 当然，他们也希望有一份新的和更新的报告，但他们认为这要么太难，要么不值得付出努力。 我认为这不是真的。 拥有最新的报告对于我们社区的健康至关重要，而且我们实际上可以通过合理的工作量在合理的时间内实现这一目标。 这是我关于如何实现这一目标以及如何在新年之前完成该过程的计划。

为什么我们需要一份新报告

Haskell 语言报告是该语言文档的重要组成部分。 这不是初学者在学习 Haskell 时应该参考的第一件事，但对于那些想要晋升为中级或有经验的 Haskell 的人来说，这是一个重要的资源。 如果您想了解浮点文字的精确语法、do 表示法的规则和脱糖，或者默认声明的含义，该报告是您可以找到答案的权威资源。 因此，如果您在报告中找到的答案是错误的，或者与编译器实现的内容或基础库提供的内容不相符，那将是不幸的。 在这种情况下，你必须回顾导致当前状态的提案和讨论：Functor-Applicative-Monad、MonadFail、Foldable-Traversable 和 Monad-of-no-return 提案无疑使语言变得更好，但它们也将在报告中寻找答案的程序员变成了不自觉的 Haskell 历史学家。

如果语言报告是您唯一可用的 Haskell 资源，那么您编写的任何重要的 Haskell 2010 程序几乎肯定与 GHC 或 MicroHS 等现代编译器所期望的不兼容。 我们可以而且应该解决这个问题。

如何权衡成本效益

编写新报告需要大量工作，我们希望避免遇到导致之前编写报告失败的问题。 因此，重要的是我们为自己设定一个既可以实现又可以为 Haskell 社区带来切实利益的目标。 最明显的目标是从修订后的 Haskell 2010 语言报告开始：

  • 修订后的报告是完全可以实现的：我们在用户指南（GHC 用户指南：错误和不愉快）中记录的差异中有一个非常清晰的“待办事项列表”。 大多数列出的差异已在已接受的提案中得到详细记录。
  • 我们必须实现的所有更改都不会引起争议：它们反映了我们今天已经编写的 Haskell。 由于所需的更改没有争议，因此我们可以在编写修订报告时使用轻量级决策流程。
  • 这对社区来说有一个明显的好处：我们的参考文档中最重要的部分不再过时。 我们可以向人们推荐哈斯克尔报告，而不必警告他们远离报告中不再适用的部分。
  • 由于我们没有定义具有新功能集的新 Haskell 版本，而只是先前报告的修订版本，因此我们不会对生态系统或编译器编写者产生任何干扰。 受到托尔金在创作《指环王》故事后重写《霍比特人》的启发，我们可以重新审视这份报告，并假装修改后的报告就是我们一直以来所说的 Haskell2010 的意思。 然后，我们可以简化 GHC 用户指南，并删除其第 16 节的大部分内容，该节记录了与现有报告相比的不妥之处。

因此，我们可以为自己设定一个目标：根据修订后的 Haskell 2010 语言报告有效的每个程序都将被使用 Haskell2010 语言版本的 MicroHS 和 GHC 接受。

让我们谈谈技术细节

动机和目标明确后，让我们讨论一下处理报告、构建报告以及生成最终 PDF 和 HTML 文档时的一些技术细节。

Haskell 2010 语言报告以 PDF 和 HTML 文档形式提供，并且没有明显的充分理由来更改此设置。 如果编写技术正确，那么处理如此复杂和冗长的 Haskell 报告文档可能会很愉快，但如果我们正在努力应对较长的编译时间（使用错误的工具和包使用 LaTeX 编译较长的 PDF 可能需要几分钟！）、难以理解的错误消息或困难的脚本和编程模型，那么工作起来就会很困难。

Haskell 报告的早期版本是使用命令行工具（sed、awk、perl、make）、用于预处理自定义 .verb 文件格式的词法分析器/解析器、用于编译 PDF 的 pdflatex 以及用于生成 HTML 的 tex4ht 的组合来编写的。 到 2026 年，我们可以使用 2010 年无法使用的技术，并显着简化报告的编写过程。 在现有的技术中，Typst排版系统目前最能满足这些限制：

  • 它是在 Apache 2.0 许可证下可用的开源软件。 （类似于 Overleaf 的相关云服务是专有的，但完全是可选的。）
  • Typst 用 Rust 实现，编译时间比 tex 快一个数量级。 这样可以在处理报告时获得即时视觉反馈。
  • 本机支持 PDF 和 HTML 输出，无需使用单独的工具。
  • 编译器会发出奇妙的错误消息，指出代码中的错误位置。
  • 更简单的技术（如纯 Markdown）也允许针对多种输出格式，但它们缺乏生成高质量技术文档的高级功能，特别是在数学和复杂数字的排版方面。

使用 Typst 意味着我们必须将报告从自定义 .verb 格式转换为 .typ 文件；幸运的是，这部分工作已经完成，并且可以使用简单的 typest 编译调用来编译报告。 （翻译过程不涉及法学硕士，并且是使用一些 sed 和 awk 魔法手动完成的，以促进该过程。） 重新排版 BNF 语法还可以使其超链接：现在可以通过单击非终结符来导航语法并跳转到其定义。

记录标准库

现有的 Haskell 2010 报告由两部分组成：第一部分记录了该语言的语法和语义，第二部分记录了标准库。 记录标准库是报告的重要组成部分，因为语言的许多方面只能根据库中可用的函数、类型和类型类来定义。 例如，数字文字是多态的，必须根据数字层次结构进行定义，do 表示法必须根据 Monad（和 MonadFail）类型类进行定义，外部函数接口 (FFI) 广泛使用在foreign.*命名空间中定义的函数和类型。

以纯文本形式（作为 LaTeX 或 Typst 文件）维护数百页标准库文档，并确保它们保持有效的 Haskell 且彼此一致是非常困难的。 如果我们想避免报告中出现拼写错误和不一致的情况，并且如果我们想保持库规范的可维护性，那么我们必须以某种易于机器检查的形式组织它。 显而易见的解决方案是使用 Haddock 记录标准库的 API。 修订后的报告的存储库包含一个 cabal 包，它公开了 Haskell 2010 语言报告中指定的精确 API。 （此包仅指定公共 API：函数和方法本身没有实现。 一个可能的扩展目标是使用 api-diff 或 print-api（链接）等工具来确保像 base 这样的包公开的 API 是报告中定义的 API 的严格超集。）

我们应该使用什么流程

Haskell Prime 流程结合使用了邮件列表讨论和收集 RFC 的 Git 存储库。 值得注意的是，该过程并不直接作用于用于构建报告的源代码。 通过切换到更紧密地模拟我们开发代码的方式的协作流程，我们可以减少大量开销：对报告的更改应主要以对报告本身的文本源的拉取请求的形式进行讨论。 用于组织报告撰写的存储库现已公开：github.com/haskellfoundation/haskell-2010-revised-report。 请通过讨论现有问题、贡献新问题以及帮助解决技术基础设施问题来开始贡献。 我们尚未将任何实际更改合并到报告中，因为这些更改需要得到将成立的新语言委员会的确认，但我们可以开始解决所有其他技术问题。

号召性用语

为了使修订后的 Haskell 2010 报告得到社区的广泛支持，我们在 Haskell 基金会的领导下成立了一个新的工作组。 我们现在需要您的帮助和参与，最好是决定成为负责编写修订报告的工作组的成员。 如果您不想成为工作组的成员，您仍然可以加入存储库中的所有讨论、贡献问题以及打开对报告进行更改的拉取请求，但成为成员后您有权投票决定应采用对报告的哪些更改。

我们很快就会宣布加入 Haskell Discourse 工作组，并很快开始修订报告的工作。 如果您一直希望 Haskell 获得新的报告，或者因标准化方面缺乏进展而感到沮丧，那么现在是您做出贡献的机会！ 通过上述明确界定的范围，我们也可以确信终点线就在眼前。 谁知道呢，如果修订后的报告取得了明显的成功，我们甚至可能有兴趣跟进一些更雄心勃勃的事情......
